stage: Independent concept guidance saved first; subsequent narrow pair confirmation appended
position: Support a bounded two-cameo experiment against the unchanged moth-only baseline. Prefer one background workshop-watching group. Inclusion is conditional on an actual small-banner comparison; no score or approval of an unbuilt variant.

count.zero: The existing scene already has three useful beats: code in front, build deeper back, rest and peek under the tree. Zero cameos preserves the strongest economy and remains the fallback.
count.two: Two small watchers clustered at the workshop can add sociability through one supporting action and one shared attention target. Treat them as one visual group, not two new stories.
count.three: One watcher plus two tree players adds two new activity groups to the three existing moth beats. It spends more attention than the proposed story requires; do not use for the first test.
count.fullCast: Do not test the full reference cast in this banner. The reference derives much of its composition from a central gathering of colorful figures and basket symbols. Distributing that many distinct forms through the existing scene would introduce numerous competing accents and identities. This is a predicted risk, not an observed failure of an unbuilt image.

staging.hardForegroundExclusion: Reserve the foreground bench, coding moth, MacBook and surrounding path completely. No cameo on, beside, behind in apparent contact with, or overlapping the bench/coder/laptop silhouette; no cameo on the foreground path or among the foreground plants.
staging.preferred: Put both companions together in deeper workshop space, on the far side of the worktable and clear of the path, with their attention converging on the builder/toolbox. Keep both clearly smaller than the builder, subordinate in contrast, and clear of the hammer, face, wings and antennae. Do not make individual logo recognition a requirement.
staging.action: One shared quiet watching action is enough. Avoid pointing in opposing directions, cheering, large arm silhouettes, speech, extra text, a logo basket or additional props that create another narrative center.
staging.treeAlternative: Two quiet players are a separate alternative, not an addition to workshop watchers. They must remain deeper in the grove, behind the resting moth's depth plane, with a clear gap from its face and roots. This is less economical: it can turn the existing peaceful peek into a reaction to a new disturbance. Preserve the resting moth's quiet beat unless that causal change is deliberately wanted.
staging.smallPresentation: At the previously measured 238px README width, this 3:1 scene would be about 79px tall. Fine faces, logo interiors and interaction details will be extremely small. Code/build/rest and the main coder's silhouette must remain understandable without decoding the cameos. Compare the actual variant and zero-cameo baseline at 846px and 238px width.

failure: Any cameo occupies the excluded foreground or visually attaches to the bench, coder or MacBook: reject that composition regardless of count.
The cameo group becomes a stronger color/contrast focus than the foreground moth, or requires enlarging figures to make logos recognizable: remove or reduce it.
Watchers obscure the builder, toolbox, hammer action or path depth, making the existing building beat harder to identify: return to zero or restage deeper.
Tree play competes with the resting moth's face/peek or adds a second energetic incident: prefer the single workshop group or zero.
At 238px the additions become disconnected colored specks with no readable supporting relationship: retain the moth-only baseline rather than enlarging the cast into the foreground.

skillsReviewed.application: Reuse lead/support hierarchy, one coherent action per supporting group, purpose before embellishment, and separation of static staging from perceived timing. Prior all-17 catalog intake remains recorded; no claim to have newly read the whole catalog or review-animations/STANDARDS.md in this pass.

workflowChanges: Compare zero and two with the existing scene held constant, then inspect actual GitHub-sized renders before accepting additional cast.
Use a hard foreground exclusion before evaluating style or charm; any candidate crossing it fails regardless of appealing details.
Judge attention groups and action count, not only the number of individual characters. Two watchers can function as one group; one watcher plus two players introduces two new groups.
rulesNotApplicableWithReason: No motion is built or watched, so timing, staggering, spring, sound and continuous comic rhythm cannot be approved from these stills.
This is a bounded concept review, not a source implementation or browser test. Root supplies generation and browser evidence; this reviewer writes only its own review record.
No numeric score, publication approval, audience-recognition claim or inferred product endorsement follows from this concept judgment.

pairConfirmation.challenge: B challenged the possible escalation from two cameos to three: a successful two-cameo render is not itself a storytelling reason to add tree play, which introduces another event and changes the existing quiet peek.
pairConfirmation.partnerResponse: A explicitly accepted the challenge. Three and full cast are outside the first test; tree play needs a separate owner-supported storytelling reason and comparison.
pairConfirmation.exactJointRecommendation: Test two small background companions watching the toolbox work as one supporting group; reserve the foreground entirely for Nag's coding scene, keep the moth-only baseline, and remove the cameos if they compete with the coder or obscure the three moth activities at banner size.
pairConfirmation.boundary: This confirms a bounded comparison to generate, not acceptance of cameos, a chosen product roster, an artwork score or publication approval.

limits: No cameo variant exists in the inspected evidence; predicted overload and proposed scale remain hypotheses until rendered.
The current park image was inspected at the supplied display size, not freshly rendered at 846px or 238px in this pass.
